description: Datasets read from Earth Engine and reduced onto the basin and administrative frames. Declared here rather than discovered, because unlike the atlas deliveries there is no archive on disk to profile: the source is a remote collection, and what the ontology can say about it has to be written down. PIPELINES/project_earth_engine_sources.py turns this into entities and assertions.

sources.label: CAMS global near-real-time atmospheric composition
sources.agentLabel: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts
sources.note: A forecast system, not an observing one. The +0h analysis is the assimilated state and is what the ontology stores; the forecast tables record how far ahead it can be believed. Only aerosol optical depth and PM2.5 exist before 2021-07-01.

derivedProducts.label: CAMS forecast skill against its own analysis
derivedProducts.description: Mean absolute error, bias and correlation by lead time. This is internal forecast-to-analysis verification, not independent validation against ground observations.

derivedProducts.label: CAMS event detection verification at Tashkent
derivedProducts.description: Event detection, false-alarm, correlation and bias metrics at one CAMS grid cell. The grid cell is not a street-level city monitor and the reference is the model analysis.

sources.label: NCEP Climate Forecast System v2, 6-hourly harmonized
sources.agentLabel: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Prediction
sources.note: Coupled model output, not observation. CFSR feeds the record to 2010 and operational CFSv2 from 2011, and 25 cm soil moisture steps 1.41 standard deviations across that boundary, so baselines stay inside the operational era.

sources.label: CHIRPS v3 precipitation
sources.agentLabel: Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara
sources.attribution: Climate Hazards Center InfraRed Precipitation with Station data v3
sources.note: Computed pentadally; the daily product is a disaggregation of it and agrees to 0.00% over a month. Version 3 sits under UCSB-CHC, not the UCSB-CHG path version 2 uses, and differs from it by about nine percent here.

sources.label: CHIRTS daily temperature
sources.agentLabel: Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara
sources.attribution: Climate Hazards Center InfraRed Temperature with Stations
sources.note: Closed: the record stops at 2016-12-31. A historical baseline rather than a monitoring layer. Its heat index column is Fahrenheit and derived from the daily mean while every other column is metric.

sources.label: CPC global unified temperature
sources.note: Gauge-based and long, but the GTS feed over Uzbekistan is thin: 0.13 stations per cell per day, with 51% of basin-months seeing none. Mostly interpolation from distant reports here, and weighted accordingly against CHIRTS.

sources.label: Global Human Modification
sources.attribution: Conservation Science Partners, global Human Modification (gHM)
sources.note: A single image with no timestamp — timeless rather than archival. Measured over both basins and districts because the frame changes the answer: 0.33 by basin against 0.61 by district.

sources.label: Impact Observatory / Esri 10 m annual land cover
sources.attribution: Impact Observatory / Esri 10 m Annual Land Use Land Cover
sources.note: Nine annual mosaics in a 9-class scheme. Area must come from pixelArea rather than a pixel count: the collection mosaics UTM tiles and the reduction falls back to a geographic projection where pixel ground area varies with latitude.
